en.summary: Connect to an external installation and distinguish inventory, incorporation and fresh reports.

sections.heading: External installation and available workflow
sections.body:
Choose this bridge when Zigbee2MQTT and its broker are managed outside SCADIVO and devices are already joined. It queries that installation; it does not open inclusion or administer the coordinator. Native Zigbee is another path.

The connector advertises connection testing, discovery and read testing. Discovery lists inventory; incorporation requires choosing what enters the project. The current UI still limits that selection. Reading some nested inventory structures also awaits a separate correction. Steps below identify those limits rather than promising a complete incorporation where unavailable.

sections.heading: Source fields
sections.body: Host, base topic and credentials must match the broker actually used by the installation. Check connectivity from SCADIVO server, not only the browser.

fields.label: MQTT broker host
fields.description: Name/IP of the broker used by the external Zigbee2MQTT installation, reachable from SCADIVO server. Not the Zigbee2MQTT UI URL or a topic.

fields.label: Broker port
fields.description: Actual broker port. The form defaults to 1883; with TLS check its corresponding port rather than assuming automatic switching.

fields.label: Use TLS
fields.description: Enables protected transport where offered by the broker. Does not install certificates or replace broker authentication.

fields.label: Base topic
fields.description: Prefix configured on external Zigbee2MQTT. The driver uses, for example, baseTopic/bridge/state and baseTopic/bridge/devices. Do not put a device friendly name here.

fields.label: MQTT client ID
fields.description: Optional; empty generates a stable ID from source identity. If set, do not reuse the same ID on another active client. Not a user name or password.

fields.label: MQTT version
fields.description: mqtt5 or mqtt311 as supported by the broker. The driver uses its own session defaults; do not copy every MQTT Raw advanced setting into this source.

fields.label: Broker user
fields.description: Account permitted on the external installation topics. Separate from SCADIVO login.

fields.label: Broker password reference
fields.description: Reference to protected material provisioned on the host for this network. The administrator supplies the reference/slot; do not paste the secret key or put it in an Engineering package. Do not replace an existing key with a new value to troubleshoot connectivity.

fields.label: Keep Alive (s)
fields.description: Broker connection supervision. Does not request sensor measurements or wake a battery device.

fields.label: Connection timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for connecting to the broker, separate from request or write-confirmation time.

fields.label: Request timeout (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a query operation. Not a polling interval for every sensor.

fields.label: Write confirmation wait (ms)
fields.description: Deadline for a matching sufficiently fresh state report after a command. MQTT acceptance without feedback does not confirm equipment state.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Initial wait after connection loss. Reducing it does not repair an offline broker or rejected authentication.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect wait (ms)
fields.description: Caps increasing wait and must be greater than or equal to minimum.

fields.label: Maximum message size (bytes)
fields.description: Limits received payload including inventories; increase only if actual documents require it and resources allow. Not history capacity.

fields.label: Connection failure limit
fields.description: Consecutive failure limit used by readiness supervision. Does not grant operation with an unreachable source.

fields.label: Maximum queued messages
fields.description: Limits the transport buffer. More messages use more memory; not persistent storage.

fields.label: Maximum inventory devices
fields.description: Inventory/selection limit for this source. Not a radio-capacity promise and does not remove license quotas.

fields.label: Maximum exposes per device
fields.description: Limits property descriptions processed per device. An expose is a function/property advertised by Zigbee2MQTT, not an automatically incorporated TAG.

sections.heading: Generated bindings and pending selection
sections.body: Technical fields below are produced by incorporation from selection/inventory. They are not IDs for the developer to invent. Until the page sends selection, listing a device does not guarantee ready Equipment/TAGs. Mapped scalar exposes are binary and numeric; functional capabilities depend on supported properties.

fields.label: IEEE, endpoint and property
fields.description: Stable address generated from IEEE, optional endpoint and property. Friendly name can change and must not become binding identity.

fields.label: Internal source identity — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Links to the saved source stable ID. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Source key — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Links to the readable source key. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: IEEE — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Normalized IEEE of the selected device, not friendly name. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Endpoint — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Endpoint advertised by the expose; may be absent. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Property — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Advertised property name such as temperature or state. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Expose type — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. binary produces Boolean TAG; numeric produces Double TAG. Other types do not become scalar TAGs through this workflow. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Advertised access — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Combinable bits: 1 state, 2 write, 4 request read. Must include 1; 5 means state plus request read. Does not grant security authorization. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Unit — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Must match the TAG unit; not an arbitrary scale conversion. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Minimum — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Advertised numeric lower bound, where supplied. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Maximum — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Advertised numeric upper bound, where supplied. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Step — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Positive numeric step where advertised; not read frequency. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: On value — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Explicit JSON value for true on a binary expose. Text ON and Boolean true have different types. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Off value — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Explicit JSON value distinct from the on value for a binary expose. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Point identity — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Combines source, IEEE, endpoint and property; copying from another source is invalid. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Equipment function — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. For example Temperature or OnOff; not a security capability granted to a user. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Confirmation contract — automatic
fields.description: Technical field generated by incorporation. Where supported requires matching non-retained state after the command with source freshness evidence. Not proof of physical actuation. Do not invent or copy IDs across sources.

fields.label: Explicit incorporation selection
fields.description: The service accepts IEEE selection, but the current Home/Building page does not send it. Without selection discovery lists inventory without incorporation content; selecting a row does not reissue the request with IEEE. UI incorporation awaits correction.

fields.label: Inventory format — current limitation
fields.description: The external format puts exposes in definition.exposes; this parser version looks for exposes at the root. A device can therefore be listed without producing TAGs. Compatibility correction is pending separately from UI selection.

sections.heading: Advertised inventory example
sections.body: The example below preserves the external format. The current parser does not extract its exposes; it demonstrates the limitation, not a completed import. Do not rewrite broker messages as an operational workaround.

sections.heading: State and quality example
sections.body: A retained message is Stale in this connector. Without source last_seen newer than the connection/bridge epoch, a report can be Uncertain even with retain false. Operation confirmation must also be newer than dispatch. Configure measurement information on the external installation and check times; receiving now does not prove measurement now. The sample instant is illustrative: use a current measurement for live tests.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot by layer
sections.body: No connection: check host/port/TLS/authentication. Connected without inventory: check baseTopic and bridge/state/devices. Inventory without incorporation: check the UI selection limit rather than recreating the network. Uncertain/Stale values: check retention, last_seen and reconnection. Unconfirmed write: check advertised access, confirmation binding, availability and fresh report; do not confirm a TAG just because the broker accepted publication.

en.title: Siemens S7: CPU, memory and first reading
en.summary: Configure ISO-on-TCP while distinguishing connection, DB access and write permission.

sections.heading: Prepare the PLC side
sections.body:
Choose a known variable in the PLC program and obtain its memory address. This S7 ISO-on-TCP driver reads absolute addresses: you need to know where the value is, not just its name. It is not full TIA symbolic browsing or an OPC UA connection.

For S7-1200/1500, confirm allowed external access, PUT/GET when required and a compatible absolute-layout DB with the administrator. DB means data block; offsets are positions inside it. Optimizations changing those positions can make the map incompatible. SCADIVO does not alter these options or replace PLC protection.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: Choose RackSlot or explicit TSAP to match the installation. A connection test negotiates a session; DB and individual point access still require verification.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port of the enabled PLC or adapter service. This driver defaults to 102. Check the firewall and actual service before changing it.

fields.label: CPU family
fields.description: Select S7300, S7400, S71200 or S71500 to match the installed CPU. Unknown does not define an operational profile. This does not enable PLC services or permissions automatically.

fields.label: How to locate the connection
fields.description: RackSlot derives the destination from rack, slot and role. ExplicitTsap uses the destination TSAP from the installation configuration. Choose one mode and fill its corresponding fields.

fields.label: Rack
fields.description: In RackSlot mode, the rack containing the CPU. This is not a project equipment number.
fields.constraints: 0–7; required in RackSlot.

fields.label: CPU slot
fields.description: In RackSlot mode, actual CPU position. Example 1 does not fit every family; check the configured hardware.

fields.label: Connection role
fields.description: In RackSlot: OperatorPanel, ProgrammingDevice or Basic, matching the PLC connection. This is not an Authority user role.

fields.label: Enable Data Source writes
fields.description: Defaults to false. Writes also require a writable binding, non-ReadOnly TAG, writable destination and permission. This does not enable PUT/GET or change CPU protection.

fields.label: Source TSAP
fields.description: Client-side identifier in the ISO session. Default 0x0100. This is not a TCP port; keep the communication configuration value.

fields.label: Destination TSAP
fields.description: Required in ExplicitTsap mode. Use the identifier configured for the PLC connection; check it before copying the example.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed to establish the connection.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: Reconnect delay
fields.description: Milliseconds before retrying a failed connection. This is not the measurement interval; zero does not fix access denial.

fields.label: Requested message size
fields.description: PDU bytes requested during S7 negotiation. Default 480; accepted size depends on the PLC. This is neither the TAG count nor database size.

sections.heading: TAG binding fields
sections.body: The SCADIVO TAG path identifies the application variable; area, DB, byte and bit locate PLC memory. Portable address and binding fields must agree.

fields.label: Memory area
fields.description: Input: inputs; Output: outputs; Merker: M memory; DataBlock: DB. Match the actual program address. Reading inputs does not make that area writable.

fields.label: DB number
fields.description: For DataBlock, nonzero block number. Outside this area use zero. The number is not a byte offset.
fields.constraints: 1–65535 for DB; zero in other areas.

fields.label: Starting byte offset
fields.description: Zero-based position within the area/DB. DB1.DBD0 starts at byte 0; Float32 occupies four bytes. Do not enter 32 by confusing bits with bytes.
fields.constraints: 0–2097151; the entire value must fit.

fields.label: Boolean bit
fields.description: Only Boolean uses bit 0–7 within the byte. Keep zero for other types; do not replace this field with the generic bit selector.

fields.label: Physical PLC type
fields.description: Choose actual storage: Boolean, Byte, SInt, UInt16, Int16, UInt32, Int32, Int64, Float32, Float64, String, WString, Date or DateTime. Float32 maps to TAG Float, Float64 to Double, text to String, dates to DateTime. A TAG name does not convert memory contents.

fields.label: Text capacity
fields.description: String/WString only: declared capacity of 1–254 characters; this is not numeric read size. Use zero for other types. Allow actual DB space for the format header.

fields.label: Allow writes to this point
fields.description: Start with false while checking reads. true only enables a point that is also writable in memory/protocol; TAG ReadOnly, session permissions and other restrictions still apply.

fields.label: Byte and word order
fields.description: The descriptor still declares Normal, ByteSwap, WordSwap and ByteAndWordSwap, but the current binding does not accept this setting or order in the address. Ordering is represented by the shared physical byte/word transform. This mismatch is part of the pending authoring correction; do not copy the catalog field into the binding as a manual solution.

fields.label: Binding authoring in this version
fields.description: The current catalog gives the generic assistant a binding identity different from the one required by the S7 Runtime. Creation through this path is rejected and awaits correction. Other fields and the example describe the correct S7 binding, not an already corrected authoring flow. Do not change internal IDs to bypass validation. The valueOrder field must also be projected to the physical transform rather than saved as an extra setting.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body: Manual creation through the current assistant encounters the binding limitation described above. The example demonstrates valid binding parameters for review; it does not instruct you to force an internal identity in the UI. For a project with an already valid S7 binding, verify the source, a known reading and quality after publishing/activating through the project workflow. A successful connection test does not establish tested reads or writes.

sections.heading: Example: REAL at the start of DB1
sections.body: Configuration example, not a complete package. The PLC program must actually store a REAL at DB1.DBD0. Expected result is a Float reading of that value with writes disabled, not a test value generated by the driver.

sections.heading: TIA import and diagnosis
sections.body: Advertised import accepts compatible PLC TAG exports in XLSX, XML and SDF; this is not a full TIA project import or TIA Openness. Review candidates, types and addresses before applying. No connection: check IP, port 102, mode, rack/slot/TSAP and permitted access. Connected without readings: check DB number, absolute layout, offset and size. Implausible value: compare type, bytes and order with the program. Rejected write: check writeEnabled, writable, ReadOnly and permission; do not relax PLC protection as a test.

en.title: Allen-Bradley Logix: routing, symbols and reads
en.summary: Use ControlLogix/CompactLogix symbolic access and check limits before importing or writing.

sections.heading: Which connection you are configuring
sections.body:
Start with a known ControlLogix or CompactLogix symbol, the named reference used by the program. Have actual IP address, profile and route, and check that the symbol permits external access.

This driver uses explicit EtherNet/IP messages for these symbols. It is not a cyclic I/O scanner for all EtherNet/IP devices or a generic SLC, PLC-5 or MicroLogix driver. Check the family before preparing the source.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: A CIP route differs from the TCP port. Identifying the controller proves neither a symbol read nor a write.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port of the enabled PLC or adapter service. This driver defaults to 44818. Check the firewall and actual service before changing it.

fields.label: Controller profile
fields.description: ControlLogix or CompactLogix to match the equipment. The profile does not automatically discover a slot or configure the PLC.

fields.label: CIP route to the CPU
fields.description: Ordered port,link hops separated by /. 1,0 represents a particular hop, not TCP port 1. Use the documented route; a direct destination may use an empty route according to profile. Do not guess additional hops.

fields.label: Read interval
fields.description: Requested milliseconds between acquisition cycles. 1000 means approximately one cycle per second, subject to network and processing time. This does not guarantee the PLC program update rate.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect delay
fields.description: Initial wait after a connection failure, in milliseconds. Must not exceed the maximum delay.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect delay
fields.description: Upper bound for progressive reconnect delay, in milliseconds. This is neither data validity nor command confirmation time.

fields.label: Points per batch
fields.description: Limits request grouping. Default 16; increasing it can raise load and message size. It does not change the licensed TAG count.

fields.label: Transport security requirement
fields.description: Unsecured is the available implementation. CipSecurityRequired is an explicit requirement rejected by this version; it neither enables CIP Security nor silently downgrades. If the installation requires CIP Security, this path does not meet that requirement.

sections.heading: Symbol binding fields
sections.body: Identity includes scope, program where applicable, path and native type. Do not copy a portable address while leaving fields aimed at a different symbol. Bool is readable; native Bool writing is not enabled in this version.

fields.label: Symbol scope
fields.description: Controller for a global symbol; Program for a program-local symbol with programName. This is not an Authority authorization scope.

fields.label: PLC program
fields.description: For Program scope, enter the actual program name. This is neither the SCADIVO application name nor the routine name.

fields.label: Symbol path
fields.description: Actual name and supported path, including member/index where applicable. Example TankLevel must exist in the PLC as REAL. Renaming the SCADIVO TAG does not rename the symbol.

fields.label: Native symbol type
fields.description: Runtime reads in this version: Bool, Sint, Int, Dint, Lint and Real, mapping to Boolean, Int16, Int16, Int32, Int64 and Float. Lreal/String may appear in the catalog/import but are not enabled for Runtime reading. Whole structures are not scalars.

fields.label: External access defined in the PLC
fields.description: ReadOnly permits reading; ReadWrite also permits compatible writing; None blocks access. Unknown does not prove write permission. This field describes the symbol; it does not change the PLC setting.

fields.label: Constant symbol
fields.description: true identifies a PLC constant and prevents writing. Do not use false to try making a constant writable.

fields.label: Physical integer bit
fields.description: Optional Boolean projection from Sint/Int/Dint/Lint: maximum indices 7/15/31/63. Not applicable to Real or Bool. It does not turn a write into a safe bit operation; check support before issuing commands. An accepted binding uses the shared physical selector, not an extra bitIndex setting; assistant projection is also pending.

fields.label: Binding authoring in this version
fields.description: Runtime stores symbolic identity in the portable address and requires empty extra settings. The current generic assistant copies the fields in this table into extra settings and its binding is rejected. Creation through this path awaits correction; the example shows a valid point contract, not a corrected assistant.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body: Manual creation through the current assistant encounters the binding limitation described above. The example shows a valid read identity for review. For a project with an already valid Logix binding, verify source, symbol, type and quality after publishing/activating. Advertised Browse/import/reconciliation services require candidate and binding review before applying; opening a file does not establish a successful import.

sections.heading: Example: read-only REAL symbol
sections.body: TankLevel must exist at Controller scope as REAL. Use a Float, ReadOnly TAG for the first check. The example does not configure a rack route for you.

sections.heading: Browse, import and reconciliation
sections.body: Online Browse enumerates Controller-level symbols with pagination; it does not promise full program browsing. Compatible L5X/L5K import can include program scope. Review supported candidates, arrays, members and External Access; a visible symbol can be incompatible. Reconcile compares identities; it does not automatically modify the PLC program. For connection failure check IP/44818 and route. For missing symbols check scope, program and name. For rejected writes check supported type, constant, External Access, ReadOnly and permission.

en.title: Mitsubishi MELSEC: profile, routing and devices
en.summary: Configure MC/SLMP and check numeric radix, value width and CPU limits.

sections.heading: Prepare the MC service
sections.body:
Ask the PLC administrator for the profile, port and one known memory position to test. A compatible MC/SLMP TCP service must be enabled on the equipment.

This profile uses binary 3E frames, the message format expected by the connection. Do not assume support for every Mitsubishi model, ASCII messages, UDP or all PLC memory. Compare the profile with actual equipment before filling addresses.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: Start with basic fields. Advanced routing and grouping must match the installation; defaults do not discover the topology automatically.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Port of the enabled PLC or adapter service. This driver defaults to 5007. Check the firewall and actual service before changing it.

fields.label: Mitsubishi family profile
fields.description: Fx5U32MtDs or IqR04EnCpu: specific memory limits, not certification of all MELSEC CPUs. If the model differs, check compatibility before use.

fields.label: Read interval
fields.description: Requested milliseconds between acquisition cycles. 1000 means approximately one cycle per second, subject to network and processing time. This does not guarantee the PLC program update rate.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed to establish the connection.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: MC monitoring timer
fields.description: Time requested in the MC frame, in 250 ms units. Default 20 equals 5 s. This differs from the local response timeout, which must allow for that time and the network.

fields.label: MC network number
fields.description: Installation MC routing; default 0 for the directly configured destination. This is not the computer Ethernet-interface number.

fields.label: MC destination station
fields.description: Frame station field. Default 255 (FF). Use the MC route value, not a Modbus Unit ID.

fields.label: Module I/O number
fields.description: Hexadecimal routing field, default 03FF. This is not an output Y address; preserve the installation value.

fields.label: Multidrop station
fields.description: Additional MC routing field; default 0. Match the actual route without confusing it with IP or the frame station.

fields.label: Words per request
fields.description: Word grouping limit, default 64. A 32-bit value occupies two words; do not confuse words with TAG count.

fields.label: Bits per request
fields.description: Bit-device read limit, default 64. Adjust according to PLC capacity and measured load.

fields.label: Sparse points per request
fields.description: Limits grouping of noncontiguous addresses, default 16. It neither creates missing addresses nor changes the memory map.

fields.label: Blocks per request
fields.description: Limits grouped blocks, default 8. More blocks do not guarantee faster reads on saturated networks or CPUs.

fields.label: Explicit R address limit
fields.description: Optional. With no value, R is disabled. Enter the maximum validated for the installed memory; the current parser still caps R at 32767. The broad field maximum does not increase that profile limit.

sections.heading: Memory and binding fields
sections.body: Bit and word devices use different storage. Check this driver’s format even if another application writes the address differently.

fields.label: Device address
fields.description: X/Y/B/W use hexadecimal numbers; M/L/D/R use decimal. D100 is a decimal word address; X10 is hexadecimal 10, not another application’s octal convention. The profile limits the allowed range.

fields.label: Physical type
fields.description: Bit for bit areas; Int16, UInt16, Int32, UInt32 or Float32 for word areas. Int32/UInt32/Float32 occupy two consecutive words. Choose a compatible TAG and preserve PLC order; UInt32 uses TAG Int64. In SCADIVO, physical Int16/UInt16 use TAG Int32; physical Int32/UInt32 use Int64; Float32 uses Float; Bit uses Boolean.

fields.label: Allow writes to this point
fields.description: Start with false while checking reads. true only enables a point that is also writable in memory/protocol; TAG ReadOnly, session permissions and other restrictions still apply.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body:
1. In Engineering > Data Sources, create the appropriate source and enter installation parameters.
2. Save and use Test connection when available. A successful connection does not prove all points.
3. In TAGs, select this source, choose a compatible type and fill the address and binding through the assistant. For manual authoring, address and fields must describe the same point; examples are not complete import packages.
4. Check a known reading using the point test when available, or after publishing/activating through the project workflow. Inspect value, quality and update in TAG Monitor.
5. Then configure a screen, alarm or authorized write. Compare the result with the PLC program and actual equipment condition.

sections.heading: Example: integer at D100
sections.body: D100 must contain a signed 16-bit integer in the PLC. Value 123 should appear as 123 in the Int32 TAG; check the raw value before applying unit conversion.

sections.heading: Targeted diagnosis
sections.body: No connection: check TCP service, port and MC routing. Invalid address: check area, decimal/hexadecimal and family limit; R needs an explicit limit. Misinterpreted value: check type and occupied words. Slow requests: compare the 250 ms MC timer units, local timeout, batches and load; do not increase everything together. A point test is not full Browse and does not certify writes or physical actuation.

en.title: Panasonic MEWTOCOL: TCP or serial and memory map
en.summary: Choose the actual transport and interpret words and contacts without mixing other protocols.

sections.heading: Choose profile and transport
sections.body:
Choose the connection for the installation: MEWTOCOL-COM TCP uses a compatible TCP service or adapter; Host Serial uses a physical port available to the SCADIVO server. They are distinct sources with their own settings.

For serial, check cable, RS-232/RS-485 electrical standard and line settings. Have the equipment memory map to select a test reading. This configuration does not turn a generic Ethernet converter into a server for every Panasonic protocol.

sections.heading: Source and binding fields
sections.body: For TCP fill host/port/connection timeout; for serial fill the port and line framing. Station, family, frame mode and acquisition apply to both. The final three fields describe the point.

fields.label: PLC address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. This is neither the browser address nor the project address.

fields.label: Adapter TCP port
fields.description: Required for TCP, with no assumed default port. Use the PLC/adapter MEWTOCOL-COM port; do not copy the Mitsubishi MC port.
fields.constraints: 1–65535; example, not a default.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed to establish the connection.

fields.label: Server serial port
fields.description: Host Serial only: device accessible to the SCADIVO service, such as COM4 on Windows or /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux. In Docker, device access and permissions belong to the container/host, not the browser.

fields.label: Serial speed
fields.description: Serial only: bits per second matching the PLC. Default 9600; this is not the read interval.

fields.label: Data bits
fields.description: Serial only: 7 or 8 to match the installation. Default 8. Together with parity and stop bits this defines serial framing.

fields.label: Parity
fields.description: Serial only: None, Odd or Even, matching the PLC. Default None. Incorrect parity can produce a timeout without an intelligible response.

fields.label: Stop bits
fields.description: Serial only: One or Two to match the PLC. Default One; do not use another driver’s values outside this list.

fields.label: Turnaround delay
fields.description: Serial only: pause in milliseconds for the line/adapter after a transaction. Default 0; adjust to actual needs, not to fix an incorrect station.

fields.label: MEWTOCOL station
fields.description: Configured PLC station, required from 1 to 99. This is neither rack slot, IP nor a Unit ID inherited from another protocol.

fields.label: Panasonic family profile
fields.description: Fp0rF32, FpXhCommon or Fp7RClassicCom. Each limits areas, addresses and writes. FP7 here is the classic COM subset, not all FP7 memory/features.

fields.label: Frame mode
fields.description: Standard is the default. Expanded increases capacity only in profiles that permit it; Fp0rF32 rejects it. It neither enables MEWTOCOL7 nor extends memory areas.

fields.label: Read interval
fields.description: Requested milliseconds between acquisition cycles. 1000 means approximately one cycle per second, subject to network and processing time. This does not guarantee the PLC program update rate.

fields.label: Response timeout
fields.description: Milliseconds allowed for a request response. Increasing this does not fix an incorrect address, route or type.

fields.label: Panasonic address
fields.description: Use an area and number admitted by the profile: contacts X/Y/R/L/T/C or words WX/WY/WR/WL/DT/LD. DT100 is a decimal word; for X/Y/R/L contacts the final digit is hexadecimal bit 0–F within a decimal group. Do not reinterpret the entire address as hexadecimal.

fields.label: Physical type
fields.description: Boolean for a contact; UInt16 or Int16 for a word, with matching TAG type. This driver does not expose a 32-bit REAL or string as though it were one 16-bit word. In this driver both physical Int16 and UInt16 use TAG Int32. Boolean uses TAG Boolean.

fields.label: Allow writes to this point
fields.description: Start with false while checking reads. true only enables a point that is also writable in memory/protocol; TAG ReadOnly, session permissions and other restrictions still apply.

sections.heading: From Data Source to a checked reading
sections.body:
1. In Engineering > Data Sources, create the appropriate source and enter installation parameters.
2. Save and use Test connection when available. A successful connection does not prove all points.
3. In TAGs, select this source, choose a compatible type and fill the address and binding through the assistant. For manual authoring, address and fields must describe the same point; examples are not complete import packages.
4. Check a known reading using the point test when available, or after publishing/activating through the project workflow. Inspect value, quality and update in TAG Monitor.
5. Then configure a screen, alarm or authorized write. Compare the result with the PLC program and actual equipment condition.

sections.heading: Example: DT100 word over TCP
sections.body: Port 9094 is only an example of a configured adapter, not a universal Panasonic default. DT100 must contain a signed 16-bit integer; the Int32 TAG should display the same number. For Host Serial replace network fields with installation serial settings.

sections.heading: Diagnose without guessing memory-map changes
sections.body: No TCP response: check service port and station. No serial response: check server device access, wiring, baud/parity/stop bits and station. Address error: compare area and profile limit, including the contact digit. Incorrect value: check Int16 versus UInt16 and word versus contact. Writes rejected in X/T/C or another protected area cannot be resolved just by changing ReadOnly. Connection and point tests do not prove all memory or physical actuation.

en.title: DNP3: association, events and commands
en.summary: Prepare communication with the remote station and check one point before configuring commands.

sections.heading: Prepare the association
sections.body:
SCADIVO queries a remote DNP3 station over TCP as master/client. That station is called an outstation. Ask its administrator for IP/port, link addresses, point list, format variations, classes and allowed operations.

A static reading may arrive through polling; events may also arrive spontaneously. Start with a known point and check the association in Runtime/Diagnostics after activating the revision. This descriptor advertises no Engineering Browse or Test connection. A missing button does not mean the driver is absent.

sections.heading: Data Source fields
sections.body: DNP3 times use hh:mm:ss durations, not other drivers’ milliseconds. Event classes are not alarm priorities. Preserve the remote association profile when adjusting advanced options.

fields.label: DNP3 transport
fields.description: Select tcp, the transport implemented by this profile. Entering a serial port as host does not turn it into serial DNP3.

fields.label: Remote station address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. The browser does not open the protocol connection.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Remote service port. Default 20000; check the station configuration and network path.

fields.label: DNP3 master address
fields.description: Local link-layer address the outstation must recognize as master. This is neither an IP, TCP port nor TAG index.
fields.constraints: 0–65519; match the remote association.

fields.label: DNP3 outstation address
fields.description: Remote station link-layer address. Even with correct IP/port, an incorrect DNP3 address prevents the expected association.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Maximum time to establish TCP; default 5 s. This is not the read interval.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: DNP3 response timeout
fields.description: Protocol response wait, default 5 s. Increasing it does not fix an incorrect link address or point index.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Minimum reconnect delay
fields.description: Initial wait after disconnect, default 1 s. Must not exceed the maximum.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Maximum reconnect delay
fields.description: Upper bound for progressive delay, default 30 s. Old commands are not retained for replay after reconnect.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Link supervision
fields.description: Default 1 minute for link supervision. A live connection does not prove a current point value. Zero is invalid; clearing a field should not automatically be interpreted as disabling the feature.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Periodic integrity scan
fields.description: Default 15 minutes. Rescans data to resynchronize the station image; this is neither Historian retention nor every event’s frequency.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Periodic Class 1 scan
fields.description: Optional, with no default interval: scans events of this class alongside unsolicited traffic. The class comes from outstation configuration, not SCADIVO alarm priority.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Periodic Class 2 scan
fields.description: Optional, with no default interval: scans events of this class alongside unsolicited traffic. The class comes from outstation configuration, not SCADIVO alarm priority.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Periodic Class 3 scan
fields.description: Optional, with no default interval: scans events of this class alongside unsolicited traffic. The class comes from outstation configuration, not SCADIVO alarm priority.
fields.constraints: Positive duration in hh:mm:ss; 00:00:05 = 5 s.

fields.label: Startup integrity — Class 0
fields.description: Includes this class in startup resynchronization; default true. Class 0 is static data; 1–3 are event classes. At least one startup class must remain enabled.

fields.label: Startup integrity — Class 1
fields.description: Includes this class in startup resynchronization; default true. Class 0 is static data; 1–3 are event classes. At least one startup class must remain enabled.

fields.label: Startup integrity — Class 2
fields.description: Includes this class in startup resynchronization; default true. Class 0 is static data; 1–3 are event classes. At least one startup class must remain enabled.

fields.label: Startup integrity — Class 3
fields.description: Includes this class in startup resynchronization; default true. Class 0 is static data; 1–3 are event classes. At least one startup class must remain enabled.

fields.label: Disable unsolicited Class 1 at startup
fields.description: Default true: requests disabling unsolicited traffic while the association is prepared. It does not delete outstation events or change their class.

fields.label: Enable unsolicited Class 1 after integrity
fields.description: Default true: requests re-enabling after startup integrity. Requires station support/configuration; selecting it does not cause a point to generate events.

fields.label: Scan available Class 1 events
fields.description: Default true: scans the class when events are reported available. It neither changes sensor sampling nor replaces the remote event queue.

fields.label: Disable unsolicited Class 2 at startup
fields.description: Default true: requests disabling unsolicited traffic while the association is prepared. It does not delete outstation events or change their class.

fields.label: Enable unsolicited Class 2 after integrity
fields.description: Default true: requests re-enabling after startup integrity. Requires station support/configuration; selecting it does not cause a point to generate events.

fields.label: Scan available Class 2 events
fields.description: Default true: scans the class when events are reported available. It neither changes sensor sampling nor replaces the remote event queue.

fields.label: Disable unsolicited Class 3 at startup
fields.description: Default true: requests disabling unsolicited traffic while the association is prepared. It does not delete outstation events or change their class.

fields.label: Enable unsolicited Class 3 after integrity
fields.description: Default true: requests re-enabling after startup integrity. Requires station support/configuration; selecting it does not cause a point to generate events.

fields.label: Scan available Class 3 events
fields.description: Default true: scans the class when events are reported available. It neither changes sensor sampling nor replaces the remote event queue.

fields.label: Resynchronize after event-buffer overflow
fields.description: Default true: requests integrity when the outstation reports event-buffer overflow. It recovers the available current image, not events already lost.

fields.label: Remote clock synchronization
fields.description: disabled is the default. lan or nonLan select the outstation-compatible DNP3 method. This can adjust the remote clock; coordinate with the station owner. It neither sets a time zone nor validates sensors automatically.

fields.label: Pending request limit
fields.description: Default 16: bounds user requests/commands queued for the association. This is not a user-license limit and does not allow replaying old commands after reconnect.

sections.heading: Point and command fields
sections.body: In TAGs select the DNP3 source and use the family/index assistant. Check TAG type and apply the binding; advanced fields describe the point contract and may require the project Engineering definition/files because the visible assistant does not expose every advanced profile. Address, family and index must agree.

fields.label: DNP3 point address
fields.description: Format dnp3:kind:index, for example dnp3:analogInput:7. The source identifies the outstation; do not repeat IP or link address in the point.

fields.label: Point family
fields.description: binaryInput/binaryOutputStatus use Boolean; doubleBitBinaryInput uses Enum; analogInput/analogOutputStatus use a compatible numeric type; counter/frozenCounter use Int32 or Int64. Family and index identify the point, not the message group number.

fields.label: Index within the family
fields.description: Outstation index from 0 to 65535; gaps are allowed. analogInput index 7 is not binaryInput index 7.

fields.label: Static representation
fields.description: Optional GxVy format. Must match family and TAG type: G30V5 is analog Float; G30V6 is Double. Variation 0 requests the device default where supported; it does not guarantee an arbitrary type.

fields.label: Event representation
fields.description: Optional. G32V7 is a timestamped analog Float example. Static and event representations must agree with family/type. Variation does not change point identity.

fields.label: Expected event class
fields.description: Optional class1, class2 or class3 for validation/diagnostics. It neither reclassifies the remote point nor represents SCADIVO alarm priority.

fields.label: Enable commands for this point
fields.description: Default false. Only binaryOutputStatus/analogOutputStatus accept commands. ReadOnly, permission and command binding still apply; setting true does not turn an input into an output.

fields.label: Select before operate
fields.description: selectBeforeOperate is the default; use directOperate only when the station and procedure permit. Direct Operate No Response is not exposed. Protocol acknowledgement does not prove physical actuation.

fields.label: Operation for true
fields.description: Binary command: latchOn, latchOff, pulseOn or pulseOff. Default latchOn. true is the user-requested value; actual operation depends on this mapping.

fields.label: Operation for false
fields.description: Same operation set; default latchOff. Check remote logic before reversing meanings, especially open/close or start/stop.

fields.label: Trip/Close indication
fields.description: none, trip or close to match equipment. Default none. This qualifier is neither an interlock nor additional switching authorization.

fields.label: Operation count
fields.description: Default 1; count carried in the binary command. This is not the SCADIVO retry count. Agree interpretation with the outstation.

fields.label: Command on-time
fields.description: Binary-command duration in hh:mm:ss, default 00:00:00. For pulses use the equipment-specified duration; this is not response timeout.

fields.label: Command off-time
fields.description: Complementary binary-command duration, default 00:00:00. This is neither alarm delay nor acquisition interval.

fields.label: Analog command type
fields.description: int16, int32, float32 or float64 must match TAG Int16, Int32, Float or Double. Command representation G41 differs from received status representation.

sections.heading: Analog reading example
sections.body: Parameter example, not a complete package. The outstation must publish analog point 7 in the stated representations. Create a read-only Float TAG; after project publication/activation compare value, quality and timestamp origin with a known measurement. Do not invent an expected value just because the association connected.

sections.heading: Binary output example
sections.body: Defines the command profile of a real output agreed with the outstation. It is not authorization to test switching on active equipment. Runtime must admit the command and the session needs the corresponding capability. Protocol command acceptance and status update are distinct evidence; check the point’s reported feedback.

sections.heading: Investigate by symptom
sections.body: No association: check IP/20000, master/outstation and network from the server. Associated without value: check family/index and startup integrity. Missing events: check class, unsolicited support, scans and remote configuration. Incompatible value: compare variation and TAG type; changing class does not fix type. An event without source time does not gain clock precision from being received now. Rejected command: check output, type, mode, permissions and association state; do not replay automatically after disconnect.

en.title: IEC 104: stations, observed points and commands
en.summary: Configure a known point and understand the observed list’s limits before operating.

sections.heading: Preparation and what Browse proves
sections.body:
Start with a known remote-station point. SCADIVO is an IEC 60870-5-104 client/master. Obtain the CA/IOA address list, types, clock settings and allowed commands. CA identifies the common address and IOA the information object; use the station list instead of guessing numbers.

Test connection proves only the scope described in its result. Browse observes a traffic window with general interrogation: results are partial, not a guaranteed scan of the whole map. A point missing from that list may still exist in the station.

sections.heading: Source and point fields
sections.body: Source timers use seconds. CA/IOA is point identity; Type ID determines interpretation and command profile is separate. Do not add Type ID to the address to bypass a configuration conflict.

fields.label: Remote station address
fields.description: IP or name reachable from the SCADIVO server. The browser does not open the protocol connection.

fields.label: TCP port
fields.description: Remote service port. Default 2404; check the station configuration and network path.

fields.label: Stations — Common Addresses
fields.description: Comma-separated decimal CA list, for example 1,2. This is the logical station address, not IP or a point IOA. A TAG’s CA must belong to this list.
fields.constraints: CA 0–65535 matching the remote profile.

fields.label: Station clock time zone
fields.description: Time-zone identifier recognized by the server for CP56Time2a interpretation. UTC is correct only when the station uses UTC. For local time configure the actual station zone; do not use the browser zone for convenience. Verify the identifier on the Windows/Linux installation.

fields.label: Request originator
fields.description: Protocol originator identifier; default 0. This is neither a login user nor an Authority capability. Match the station profile.

fields.label: t0 — connection
fields.description: Connection-establishment timeout in seconds. Default 30.

fields.label: t1 — transmission supervision
fields.description: Supervised acknowledgement wait, default 15 s. Must exceed t2.

fields.label: t2 — receive acknowledgement
fields.description: Delayed acknowledgement limit, default 10 s; must be lower than t1. This is not alarm delay.

fields.label: t3 — idle supervision
fields.description: Idle-session supervision, default 20 s. This is not measurement expiry.

fields.label: k — send window
fields.description: Maximum unacknowledged information units. Default 12; not a TAG count. Match the remote profile.

fields.label: w — acknowledgement window
fields.description: Reception acknowledgement threshold, default 8; must not exceed k. It does not increase the available point count.

fields.label: Point CA
fields.description: Common Address containing the point. Use an address configured in the source; points with the same IOA and different CA are distinct.

fields.label: Point IOA
fields.description: Information Object Address from the station point list. The assistant generates ca=1;ioa=100 for the example; this is not the table row number.

fields.label: Monitored information type
fields.description: MSpNa1/MSpTb1 use Boolean; MDpNa1/MDpTb1 use Enum; MBoNa1/MBoTb1 use Int32; MMeNb1/MMeTe1 use Int16; MMeNa1/MMeTd1 and MMeNc1/MMeTf1 use Float. A normalized family is not automatically volts or bar. Compatible timestamped/untimestamped types still refer to the same CA/IOA.

fields.label: Command type
fields.description: For writable TAGs only: CScNa1 Boolean, CDcNa1 Enum, CSeNa1/CSeNc1 Float or CSeNb1 Int16. Must match the monitored type and remote profile; it does not turn an input into an output.

fields.label: Command execution mode
fields.description: direct or sbo to match the station. The assistant starts with sbo when no option is saved; the configuration descriptor declares direct as default. Choose the intended mode explicitly. sbo selects before operating; it does not replace process interlocks.

fields.label: Command qualifier
fields.description: Value 0–31, default 0, matching remote operation. This is neither alarm priority nor a user role.

sections.heading: First reading of a known point
sections.body:
1. Create/save the source and test the server-side connection.
2. Use Browse to check observed points, or the station point list for manual authoring. Review candidates before applying.
3. In TAGs select the source and open the IEC 104 assistant; enter CA, IOA and a compatible monitored type. Start with a read-only TAG.
4. Publish/activate through the project workflow and inspect value, quality and time in TAG Monitor. The station must actually supply the example point; parameters do not generate a fictitious measurement.

sections.heading: Compatible command profile
sections.body: This example configures the same point as a Float setpoint using select before operate. Use it only if the station defines that CA/IOA for the command. Permission, Runtime admission, protocol confirmation and process feedback are distinct checks. Do not enable writing just to remove an incompatible-type message.

sections.heading: Layered diagnosis
sections.body: No session: check IP/2404 and APCI parameters, including t2 < t1 and w ≤ k. Session without points: check requested CA, general-interrogation completion, observation window and station point list. Incompatible value: check IOA and Type ID family; normalized, scaled integer and Float are not interchangeable. Shifted time: check station clock, configured zone and CP56Time2a validity; changing only the browser clock does not correct data. Rejected/ambiguous command: check type, mode, qualifier and session state; timeout does not prove the station did not operate.

en.title: Modbus Server: publish TAGs over TCP or RTU
en.summary: Build a bounded map and distinguish external clients, internal writes and current values.

sections.heading: Server differs from master
sections.body:
Use Server when another system needs to query values published by SCADIVO. Here the external client asks and SCADIVO answers with TAGs mapped to Holding Registers. The source does not query a remote PLC.

To forward a value received through another driver, create a Server target TAG and a compatible Gateway route. The route carries the value to that target; a TAG does not gain two sources. TCP listens on an interface/port; RTU responds through the server’s serial port.

sections.heading: Source and map fields
sections.body: Network fields belong to TCP; line fields belong to RTU. Ranges and bindings define the same map model. The range editor does not automatically convert other tools’ 40001 reference labels.

fields.label: TCP server local interface
fields.description: Local listening address, not a remote PLC IP. Default 0.0.0.0 listens on IPv4 interfaces; 127.0.0.1 restricts to the host. In Docker also check published ports and container networking. Inside a container, 127.0.0.1 is the container loopback, not the host computer loopback.

fields.label: TCP listening port
fields.description: Default 502. The example uses 1502 for a test installation; the external client must use the same reachable port. Another source/process cannot occupy the same endpoint.

fields.label: Served Unit ID
fields.description: Identifier accepted by the server, default 1. TCP accepts 0–247; RTU uses 1–247. Binding Unit ID must match the source. This is not an IP address.

fields.label: Holding Register ranges
fields.description: Use the structured start/end editor. Inclusive zero-based ranges without overlap: v1:0-9 represents ten registers. Every register of a value must fit in one range; a range does not create TAGs automatically.
fields.constraints: Up to 32 ranges and 16384 total registers; addresses 0–65535.

fields.label: Concurrent TCP clients
fields.description: TCP only: maximum connections, default 16. This is neither licensed View count nor user authorization.

fields.label: TCP client idle timeout
fields.description: TCP only: maximum wait for the next request, default 30000 ms. This is not TAG update rate.

fields.label: Server RTU port
fields.description: RTU only: device accessible to the service on Windows/Linux/container, such as COM4 or /dev/ttyUSB0. It is exclusive while the server is active; do not share it with a master controlling the same physical port.

fields.label: RTU line speed
fields.description: Bits per second matching the master and other devices. Default 9600; not server polling.

fields.label: RTU data bits
fields.description: Default 8; match the actual line. The field range does not guarantee every combination is accepted by the adapter/host.
fields.constraints: 5–8; check the installation.

fields.label: RTU parity
fields.description: None, Odd, Even, Mark or Space; default None. Must match the master and port support.

fields.label: RTU stop bits
fields.description: One, OnePointFive or Two; default One. Use a combination valid for the line and host, not the register count.

fields.label: RTU frame completion timeout
fields.description: Default 1000 ms to receive the rest of a frame after traffic starts. This is not measurement interval.

fields.label: TAG address in the map
fields.description: Use zero-based holding:N in this server. Tools using reference labels often call holding:0 40001; verify the client convention. Coils/Input Registers are outside this profile.

fields.label: Binding Unit ID
fields.description: Optional: uses the source when omitted. In Server mode an override must equal the served Unit ID; it does not create multiple stations in one map.

fields.label: Register value type
fields.description: Boolean/Int16/UInt16 use one register; Int32/UInt32/Float32 use two; Int64/UInt64/Float64 use four. Physical type, TAG type and width must be compatible. The example uses physical Int16 and an Int16 TAG without conversion.

fields.label: Word order
fields.description: HighWordFirst is default; LowWordFirst reverses words of multiregister values. Match the client. A one-word Int16 has no two words to reverse.

fields.label: Value multiplier
fields.description: Default 1: engineering value = raw × scale + offset. Must be finite and nonzero. Publishing to registers uses the inverse conversion; do not apply the same scale again in the client.

fields.label: Value offset
fields.description: Amount added after multiplication, default 0. This is not an address offset and does not change holding:0.

fields.label: External client writes
fields.description: ReadOnly is default; ReadWrite enables external writes to this mapped TAG. It is separate from ReadOnly governing internal SCADIVO writes. Modbus does not request a SCADIVO login on each request; plan network access and the permitted map before enabling ReadWrite.

sections.heading: Publish and verify a read
sections.body:
1. Create the TCP or RTU Server source and configure interface/line, Unit ID and ranges.
2. TCP Test connection temporarily reserves and releases the local interface/port; RTU tests opening/exclusive line reservation and releases it. Neither proves a remote client read nor leaves the server active.
3. In TAGs select the Server source and Modbus assistant. Choose Holding Register, zero-based address and type; start with external access ReadOnly. Allow internal TAG writes if it receives Gateway data or authorized internal writes.
4. Publish/activate. Feed a known value into the TAG and verify its update in Monitor. In the external client read the corresponding Unit ID/address; check type and order.

sections.heading: Expected example and restart behavior
sections.body: After an authorized internal write of 123, the client should read 123 at holding:0, Unit ID 1, port 1502. A value does not appear automatically because it is in the example. The in-memory map starts at zero: reading zero does not prove the TAG received a current sample, and registers do not automatically carry TAG quality/time. After restart check map feeding; this is neither Historian nor guaranteed retentive memory.

sections.heading: External writes and diagnosis
sections.body: An allowed range does not permit arbitrary writes: every written register must belong to an externally ReadWrite mapped TAG. The server rejects partial multiregister values, unmapped gaps, overlapping TAGs and out-of-range spans. FC03 reads allow 1–125 registers; FC06 writes one register and FC16 writes 1–123 registers; an operation must preserve each complete value. No listener: check port conflicts, interface, firewall and Docker. Incorrect reads: check Unit ID, zero base, type/order and actual fed value. Rejected internal write: check ReadOnly/permission; rejected external write: check clientAccess and complete map.

en.title: Matter Wi-Fi: prepare and understand the test version
en.summary: Check availability, prepare the source and distinguish reading an already-commissioned attribute from pairing a device.

sections.heading: Start with availability
sections.body:
Before configuring, check whether Matter Wi-Fi is available in your installation. SCADIVO is multiplatform, but this connector is an isolated preview for a Linux x64 host with a local helper process called a sidecar. It is not Matter availability for every installation.

The default composition does not offer the type. It appears only when the administrator enables preview in Development/Test, without HA. If absent from Data Sources, check eligibility with that administrator; do not choose another driver to imitate it. Help remains available to explain these limits.

sections.heading: What you can prepare
sections.body: The current version handles persistent attributes of already-commissioned Matter Wi-Fi devices. Commissioning means adding the device to a Matter logical network, called a fabric. Creating a source or host key does not perform that pairing. This connector has no commissioning wizard, Thread, device administration, Browse, Discover or Test connection. Attribute read/write does not imply support for every device command. Keep the test-version designation; future qualification is unfinished.

sections.heading: Before opening the editor
sections.body:
Ask the administrator for the numbers identifying the point: node, endpoint, cluster and attribute, plus actual value type. These are not the internal TAG ID.

Node identifies the device in the Matter logical network, called a fabric. Endpoint identifies a function, such as an output. Cluster groups service functions and attributes, such as On/Off. An attribute is one value in that group, such as on/off state. A device can have several endpoints; check its numbers rather than copying another unit’s.

The host needs the sidecar and IPv6 network prepared. The declared dependency requires Node.js 22.13+ or 24+. Container networking can differ from the machine. Fabric and encrypted storage stay on the host: .escadapkg import neither transfers them nor recovers a lost key. This procedure asks for no keys or credentials in project fields.

sections.heading: Prepare the source and host key
sections.body: 1. In an eligible isolated environment, open Engineering → Data Sources and create a Matter Wi-Fi source. Give it a readable name. 2. Check changes and apply the source to the Workspace; this is not publication/activation. 3. Select the applied source. In its Matter key panel, choose Create host key and confirm. Apply pending edits first: the button is unavailable while the source differs from its applied state. 4. Wait for the response and page refresh. The expected result is the configured-key indication; the button then offers Verify host key. 5. Continue TAG preparation, review, Save, Publish and Activate only a validated candidate. Creating/verifying a key does not contact devices or prove communication. The operation requires Engineering modification permission and the current Workspace version.

sections.heading: Understand fields and references
sections.body: The source accepts no public host, port or generic protocol settings. Its protected reference is prepared through the host action. The other items below explain a TAG binding; the technical example is neither a complete package nor an import form.

fields.label: Fabric storage key
fields.description: Protects local Matter storage. Use the host action; do not enter a key, password or path.
fields.constraints: Host reference; the secret is never displayed or exported.

fields.label: TAG source
fields.description: Associate the point with the prepared Matter source. Naming a source does not discover a device.
fields.constraints: The association must identify the same source as the binding.

fields.label: TAG type
fields.description: Match the actual attribute type; Boolean fits an on/off state.
fields.constraints: Boolean, Int16, Int32, Int64, Float, Double or String; do not assume other types.

fields.label: Read only
fields.description: Start with reads to check value and quality before testing actuation.
fields.constraints: Allowing TAG writes grants neither user permission nor device-attribute writability.

fields.label: Attribute address
fields.description: Assemble the four real numbers in the shown format; not an IP address or pairing code.
fields.constraints: Unsigned decimal without leading zeros; node 1 through UInt64 maximum, endpoint UInt16, cluster/attribute UInt32.

fields.label: Communication binding
fields.description: Declares the representation identity and version understood by Runtime. Address text alone does not create this object.
fields.constraints: The current generic assistant does not build this binding when the catalog declares no point fields; no complete graphical procedure is promised here.

fields.label: Contract version
fields.description: Identifies the binding-object format, not the commercial Matter version.
fields.constraints: The current binding contract is 1.

fields.label: Schema identity
fields.description: Identifies the Matter interpretation of the address; this is technical reference.
fields.constraints: Do not substitute the source configuration schema.

fields.label: Schema version
fields.description: Specifies how binding content is interpreted.
fields.constraints: The current planner accepts Matter schema v1.

fields.label: Address inside the binding
fields.description: Repeats the complete attribute identity inside the binding.
fields.constraints: When Address is provided, it must equal PortableAddress.

fields.label: Extra settings
fields.description: Do not add generic configuration to work around a binding failure.
fields.constraints: Source/point Settings, selectors and nonidentity transforms are rejected in this version.

fields.label: Point count
fields.description: Keep only persistent TAGs you intend to exercise on this source.
fields.constraints: 1 through 512 associated TAGs with valid internal identities; node numbers do not replace those IDs.

sections.heading: On/off attribute example
sections.body: This is only a configuration excerpt for explaining identity and validating the contract. Node 123 is fictional and need not exist on your network. Cluster 6/attribute 0 represents an On/Off state when the device provides it at endpoint 1. The controlled environment supplies internal IDs and the host-prepared reference. Do not paste this as an .escadapkg or add a key. Planner acceptance checks configuration, not connection, real values or quality. Today an Address field alone and the key action do not complete binding authoring in the interface; a technical candidate must be prepared/validated within the controlled exercise.

sections.heading: Reading, writing and operational safety
sections.body: After activating a valid configuration in the exercise, inspect Diagnostics and the Runtime TAG: value, quality and sample time. Displayed zero/false without a valid sample does not prove the lamp is off. Before writing, confirm attribute writability and that the TAG, Authority and session class allow the action. Attribute value writes use ProcessValueWrite; do not reinterpret this as CommandExecute or promise unimplemented device commands. Check the actual result and feedback read. A screen button and a created key do not confirm actuation.

sections.heading: Investigate by symptom
sections.body: Missing type: check preview availability and absence of HA. Missing key: apply the source and use the host action; editing a JSON reference does not create a key. Disabled button: unapplied edits or an operation is in progress. Binding required: the address was entered without CommunicationBinding. Invalid address: check order, numbers, bounds and absence of leading zeros. Incompatible schema: check Matter schema and version 1. Activation rejected in HA: this version does not support that mode; do not bypass validation. Configuration accepted but no samples: check sidecar, host storage, network and already-commissioned attributes. Never recreate a key as the first recovery attempt for an existing fabric. Lost key/state requires planned recovery with the owner; an engineering file cannot restore these secrets.

en.title: Runtime session: view, interact and end
en.summary: Understand when you can watch the application and when you can operate its controls.

sections.heading: Watch or operate
sections.body: Choose View only to follow values/states. Request Interactive to use process controls. This is a request to the server: always check Granted for the actual result. Your account must also have permission for the action. Interactive does not give a person access to equipment they were not authorized to use.

sections.heading: Check your session
sections.body: 1. Sign in and open Runtime. 2. Open the account menu in the header and find Runtime session class. 3. Choose View only to observe or Interactive to operate. 4. Wait. Requested shows your request; Granted shows the effective response. 5. If you requested Interactive but received View only, read the notice before attempting a command. Interactive capacity may be unavailable. Ask the owner to check the reason when needed.

sections.heading: Example: you see the pump but cannot command it
sections.body: First check Granted. View only allows observation, not operation. If it says Interactive, check your account’s permission for that pump/action. If both are correct, inspect the command message and communication diagnostics. Work through one cause at a time: session class does not fix a TAG binding or equipment failure.

sections.heading: Change class or end
sections.body: Choose another class in the same panel to change it. The previous session is released before the new request. If that fails, you may need to request a session again; the previous one is not automatically retained. To finish, choose End session and wait for confirmation. Closing the menu only hides the panel. Signing out is separate. After a connection failure, confirm release with the owner; closing a window is not confirmation.

sections.heading: Look up controls and notices
sections.body: The server supplies results. You do not type session numbers or IDs. Open technical details only when explaining a rejection to the person responsible.

fields.label: View only
fields.description: Requests a session for monitoring the application, without operational commands or writes.
fields.constraints: Not anonymous login; does not change account permissions.

fields.label: Interactive
fields.description: Requests interactive capacity from the server. Check the granted class before operating.
fields.constraints: May be rejected or fall back to View only; does not guarantee the action.

fields.label: Requested
fields.description: Shows the class requested by this client.
fields.constraints: Does not prove the effective class.

fields.label: Granted
fields.description: Shows the effective class of the admitted session. This is the result to check.
fields.constraints: If different from Requested, read the notice; fallback is not interactive success.

fields.label: Admission reason
fields.description: Technical detail of the server decision. Open Technical details when investigating admission.
fields.constraints: Diagnostic code, not an editable configuration or bypass.

fields.label: Capacity reason
fields.description: Helps explain session availability/limits. Check licensing and occupied sessions after a capacity rejection.
fields.constraints: Capacity is not Authority permission.

fields.label: End session
fields.description: Releases the current Runtime session after the server confirms.
fields.constraints: Not Sign out; closing the menu does not end the session either.

fields.label: Error or notice
fields.description: Read the admission, end or fallback message before repeating the action.
fields.constraints: A network failure does not confirm release or a new grant.

sections.heading: When admission is rejected
sections.body: Record message, time and attempted action. Permission changes or restoration may require signing in/requesting a session again. Do not copy session IDs/headers to obtain access. In permission details, ProcessValueWrite means value writing and CommandExecute means command execution. They are different authorizations. Licensing limits available features; account permissions determine which actions you may use.

en.title: Diagnostics: locate the first cause of failure
en.summary: Interpret host health, communication, network and TAG quality before changing a screen or driver.

sections.heading: Choose the right layer
sections.body: A frozen screen may result from session, active revision, communication, TAG or presentation. Diagnostics gathers evidence; opening the panel neither restarts a source nor changes the process. In Engineering, open communication diagnostics. It observes Runtime / Active Revision: a source created only in Working need not appear yet. Start with the API/DriverHost host, then source, network/protocol, sample and screen. Address the first upstream divergence before changing a color or inserting a fixed display value.

sections.heading: Check a source step by step
sections.body: 1. Record TAG/source name, time, user and failed action; confirm the active revision. 2. Check API / DriverHost host and Observed. Unavailable/stale host evidence does not confirm current source states. 3. Clear search or enter part of the source, driver or endpoint. Start with All or Needs attention. 4. Select the source. Read state, Last error, last success/failure and data age. 5. Compare quality and counters across two observations; an accumulated total does not date each failure. 6. Use network reachability, Connection Test or Test Read only where available and needed. 7. Return to the TAG and confirm value, quality, time and updates; then check the screen dynamics.

sections.heading: Search, refresh and observation trust
sections.body: Filters affect the displayed list only. Disabling panel refresh does not stop a driver or acquisition.

fields.label: Search Data Source, driver or endpoint
fields.description: Matches part of source name/key, driver type or endpoint.
fields.constraints: Does not create a source; clear it when the list seems empty.

fields.label: Filter
fields.description: All shows available sources; Needs attention includes nonhealthy states; Healthy only shows confirmed healthy sources.
fields.constraints: No match can be just a filter. Inactive and filtered-out sources differ.

fields.label: Automatic refresh
fields.description: Updates panel observations every 3 seconds while enabled.
fields.constraints: Does not change driver scan, retention or acquisition.

fields.label: Refresh now
fields.description: Requests a fresh diagnostic reading. Wait before comparing.
fields.constraints: Does not restart or manually reconnect the driver.

fields.label: API / DriverHost host — Observed
fields.description: Check whether the process-health observation is still recent.
fields.constraints: Stale/unavailable host evidence makes source states unconfirmed in the panel.

fields.label: Panel totals
fields.description: Source, healthy, attention, fault and Good TAG totals orient the initial review.
fields.constraints: Do not replace individual errors or prove every point is healthy.

sections.heading: Read operational state and counters
sections.body: Missing values appear as a dash in several indicators; a dash is neither zero nor success. Runtime instance distinguishes executions: restarting/recreating can make accumulated totals incomparable. Cycles count acquisition executions; requests are protocol requests. Successes/failures count operation outcomes, while consecutive failures highlight the recent sequence without recovery. Timeouts are operations that did not finish by their deadline. Connections, disconnections and reconnects help assess link stability. Reads/writes count operations, not necessarily distinct TAGs. Published updates count values passed to Runtime, not guaranteed Historian persistence. Interpret each indicator for that driver and the same interval/instance; protocols need not count everything identically.

fields.label: State
fields.description: Healthy, degraded, reconnecting, faulted or stopped directs investigation; also read Last error.
fields.constraints: A reachable endpoint does not replace driver state.

fields.label: Endpoint
fields.description: Destination associated with the selected source. Check it is the intended device.
fields.constraints: May be serial or a local bridge; not every endpoint is TCP host/port.

fields.label: Last success
fields.description: When communication succeeded. Compare with now and the expected cadence.
fields.constraints: An old success does not prove a current point.

fields.label: Last failure
fields.description: Locates a reported failure in time. Compare with later success.
fields.constraints: Alone does not say whether failure continues.

fields.label: State change
fields.description: When the reported state changed.
fields.constraints: Not necessarily a process-sample timestamp.

fields.label: Data age
fields.description: Helps detect missing updates. Compare with expected source behavior/scan.
fields.constraints: Not every source is cyclic; check acquisition mode before declaring a defect.

fields.label: Configured scan
fields.description: Configured cadence where applicable.
fields.constraints: Not edited here; event-driven updates may behave differently.

fields.label: Latency and last cycle
fields.description: Average/last latency and last scan duration help distinguish slowness from absent updates.
fields.constraints: Operation duration is not full sensor-to-pixel delay.
